# Kettlebell swings

## Bells and where they live
16 kg and 20 kg Kettlebell Kings competition-style bells in the back hallway, bought October 2024 ($139 and $165, the 20 kg was on sale). The 24 kg is at the YMCA. Dev calls the hallway "the dungeon".

## Russian vs American
- Russian swing: bell floats to chest height, arms are just ropes. This is the one I do.
- American swing: overhead. Rafael says skip it, too much lower back extension at the top, and with my history ([[Lower back pain]]) not worth it.

## Technique notes
- hike pass high between the thighs, wrists close to the groin (yes)
- hip snap, glutes and quads lock at the top, plank standing up
- let the bell float, don't lift it with the shoulders
- exhale sharply at the top, "tssss"
- on the backswing wait for the bell to come to you before hinging, otherwise it turns into a squat swing
- it's a hinge like the deadlift, but the opposite feel: deadlift grinds from the floor, the swing is all about speed. Notes on the grinding one in [[Deadlift form]]

## Sessions
- Friday mornings, after nights excluded
- EMOM 10 minutes × 15 swings with the 20 kg = 150 swings, about 14 minutes with warmup
- or Simple & Sinister style: 10 × 10 one-arm swings, 5 min goal. My best with the 20 kg is 5:48 on 2025-09-12. Next goal is the 24 kg.
- HR peaks around 165 by the end, which surprised me, it's real cardio. On rainy weeks I swap the second run for swings plus [[Rowing machine intervals]]

## Counting swing reps
I lose count past 12, so I use the timer and count by tens on the fingers. 2025 total so far (from the training sheet): 9,840 swing reps, aiming for 12,000 by December 31.
